p1-t1.notes: Audit-only, no files changed except tracker/progress/SEO.md. Prior session claimed p1-t1 was started but this file showed status=todo/notes empty, so treated as a fresh audit per 'these files are source of truth, not prior chat'. Singapore = primary market for this audit. Full ranked findings (repeat in chat for 2026-09-08 session): CRITICAL: (1) Pure CSR, no SSR/prerender/SSG (vite.config.ts has no such plugin, all routes React.lazy-split) -> non-JS crawlers (most AI bots: GPTBot/ClaudeBot/PerplexityBot, Googlebot's first pass) see only the homepage's static title/description/canonical from index.html for every URL, and an empty #root until JS runs. Root cause for p1-t2. (2) vercel.json catch-all rewrite '/(.*)-> /index.html' means every unknown/broken URL returns HTTP 200 (soft 404); NotFound.tsx only sets noindex client-side after hydration. (3) src/app/App.tsx lines 393 & 411: homepage hero is two unconditional <h1> tags reading 'The Free Centre' / 'For Tuition Centres' - the word 'Free' is NOT behind SHOW_FREE_MESSAGING (src/app/flags.ts, currently false) unlike the sentence right below it, so an unapproved free/zero-cost claim sits in the strongest on-page SEO signal, contradicting CLAUDE.md and product-facts.md pricing rules. HIGH: (4) Heading hierarchy broken sitewide - App.tsx has 2x <h1>; Features.tsx, Pricing.tsx, Contact.tsx, About.tsx have 0x <h1> (start at <h2>). (5) Zero schema.org structured data anywhere (no Organization/SoftwareApplication, no FAQPage despite FAQ accordions on Home/Features/Pricing/Contact, no BreadcrumbList despite breadcrumb UI in FeatureDetail.tsx) - large miss given this project's explicit GEO/AI-search mandate. (6) /pricing is orphaned (no internal links since 2026-09-07, removed from sitemap.xml) but has no noindex in Pricing.tsx's setPageMeta call and isn't blocked in robots.txt - stays crawlable/indexable. (7) No hreflang/locale-alternate tags; og:locale hardcoded 'en_MY' sitewide (index.html) despite Singapore being an active/primary market - no market-specific head signal for SG at all. MEDIUM: (8) /features/ai (live via the dynamic /features/:featureId route, src/app/FeatureDetail.tsx) is missing from public/sitemap.xml (the other 5 static feature routes are listed, ai is not). (9) about-us-img-2.png (436KB) and about-us-img-3.png (340KB) on About.tsx are unoptimized PNG not WebP - page-weight/LCP risk on the page carrying the Singapore market-proof section. (10) No confirmed canonical-host enforcement (www vs apex) at Vercel/DNS level for when the custom domain connects; meta canonical already hardcodes non-www so risk is low but unverified. LOW: (11) public/og-image.png (1.7MB) is dead/unreferenced (og-image.webp is what's actually used) - cleanup only. (12) AppPremium.tsx (confirmed dead code, unrouted) still carries stale Singapore/Malaysia FAQ copy - flag so it isn't resurrected as-is. (13) Terms.tsx governing-law clause names only Malaysia even though Singapore is called primary market for this audit - legal/content flag, not a technical SEO defect. Recommended implementation order: rendering-strategy decision+rollout (p1-t2, fixes CRITICAL #1/#2) -> heading-hierarchy fix bundled with that template work (#3/#4, #3 needs Kenneth's copy approval since it's a claims change) -> structured data pass (#5, pairs with p2 metadata/schema phase) -> noindex or remove /pricing (#6) -> add /features/ai to sitemap (#8) -> Singapore locale/hreflang strategy (#7, likely part of p1-t2/p3 market decisions) -> image optimization on About (#9, pairs with p1-t4 CWV baseline) -> pre-launch cleanup: og-image.png removal (#11), canonical-host redirect confirmation (#10). No website/code files were modified for this task.

p1-t2.notes: Decision-only, no code/config changes made (per this task's own 'do not implement yet' instruction) and no website files touched. RECOMMENDED DECISION: adopt build-time static prerendering via a custom post-build headless-browser snapshot script (Puppeteer/Playwright using puppeteer-core + @sparticuz/chromium rather than full puppeteer, to avoid a large Chromium download on every Vercel build) -- NOT vite-react-ssg, NOT a React Router v7 framework-mode migration. Why: (a) vite-react-ssg's own maintainers now recommend RR7 projects use RR7's native framework-mode SSG instead, so vite-react-ssg is a legacy/RR6 path, not the supported one for this repo (already on react-router 7.18.2). (b) RR7's native prerender is a Framework Mode feature requiring @react-router/dev + a react-router.config.ts + converting off the current library-mode BrowserRouter setup in src/main.tsx -- a much larger architectural migration than needed for a mostly-static marketing site, and out of proportion to 'the safest strategy for this EXISTING architecture' per the task prompt. (c) Both Node-based options (vite-react-ssg and RR7 framework prerender) execute the app in a Node/SSR-like pass where window is undefined -- and src/main.tsx instantiates Lenis smooth-scroll unconditionally at module scope with no typeof window guard, plus Framer Motion scroll hooks (useInView/useScroll in App.tsx, HeroScroll.tsx) assume a real browser; both would very likely crash or need nontrivial guarding work under a Node-based prerenderer. A Puppeteer/Playwright snapshot instead runs the REAL client bundle in REAL headless Chrome after a normal `vite build`, so none of that code needs to change -- zero source-level blast radius, fully decoupled from the RR7 library-vs-framework question. EXACT ROUTES TO PRERENDER (pending final confirmation in p1-t3's route-classification table): / (App), /features, /features/enrolment, /features/class-management, /features/payroll-leave-management, /features/billing-payments, /features/parent-communication, /features/reporting, /features/ai (concrete slug of the dynamic /features/:featureId route), /about, /contact, /privacy, /terms, plus a dedicated /404.html snapshot of NotFound.tsx for Vercel's error document. /features-new stays CSR/skippable (noindex draft, not urgent to prerender). /pricing prerender status should follow whatever p1-t1 finding #6 resolves to (noindex-and-skip vs keep-and-prerender) -- Kenneth's call. BUILD APPROACH (documented, not implemented): 1) add puppeteer-core + @sparticuz/chromium as devDependencies and a new scripts/prerender.mjs; 2) change package.json build script from 'npm run typecheck && vite build' to 'npm run typecheck && vite build && node scripts/prerender.mjs'; 3) prerender.mjs serves dist/ locally (vite preview or a tiny static server), visits each route above in headless Chrome, waits for networkidle plus an explicit app-ready signal (title-changed / a window.__PRERENDER_READY__ flag set post-first-paint, since Lenis's rAF loop can defeat naive networkidle detection), captures document.documentElement.outerHTML, writes it to dist/<route>/index.html (and dist/404.html for NotFound), and hard-fails the build (non-zero exit) if any route errors so a broken prerender can never ship silently; 4) update vercel.json to remove/narrow the blanket '/(.*) -> /index.html' rewrite now that real static files exist per route, and wire dist/404.html as the real error document -- this is also the fix for p1-t1 finding #2 (soft 404s), since Vercel's default static-file 404 behavior returns a genuine HTTP 404 once the catch-all no longer swallows every path; 5) verify locally (npm run build, inspect a couple of dist/<route>/index.html files for real rendered content/meta, curl -I an unknown path in vercel dev to confirm real 404), then deploy to a PREVIEW url only -- never master -- for further verification before any production approval request. RISKS documented: build-time increase (~15 headless-Chrome page visits per build); Vercel build-container Chromium bundling/caching needs empirical verification (puppeteer-core + @sparticuz/chromium is the lighter-weight, more Vercel-friendly combo vs full puppeteer's bundled download, per current guidance); Lenis's continuous rAF loop may prevent naive 'networkidle' detection, needs an explicit ready-signal instead; Footer's `{new Date().getFullYear()}` copyright year gets baked into the static snapshot at build time (self-heals on next deploy, cosmetic only). REJECTED ALTERNATIVES: (A) stay CSR-only / do nothing -- rejected, does not address CRITICAL findings #1/#2. (B) vite-react-ssg -- rejected, de-prioritized by its own maintainers for RR7 projects. (C) React Router v7 framework-mode migration + native prerender -- not rejected outright, flagged as the officially-blessed LONGER-TERM path worth revisiting only if the site later needs real per-request SSR/personalization/auth; too large a migration for the current need. ROLLBACK PLAN: every change is additive tooling (new devDependencies, new scripts/prerender.mjs, one package.json script line, one vercel.json rewrite/error-doc change) -- no component/runtime logic changes, so a plain git revert of those commits fully restores current CSR-only behavior with zero residual/stateful risk. Any rollout must go through a Vercel preview deploy first per this repo's existing safety rules; production (master) requires Kenneth's explicit approval as always. Next planned task: p1-t3 (classify every route as INDEX/NOINDEX/REMOVE-REDIRECT, explicitly reviewing /features-new and /pricing) -- awaiting Kenneth's go-ahead.

p1-t4.notes: Ran a real local production build (npm install, since node_modules was missing -- an earlier session's ls check was a false positive -- then npm run build) and served it with `vite preview` on localhost:4173, measured via the browser's real Performance/Resource Timing APIs. No source files changed. BUNDLE SIZES (from actual vite build output, most reliable data point): shared/every-page cost = index-*.js 210.14kB/68.21kB gzip (react/router/vendor runtime) + a chunk literally named seo-*.js 174.48kB/56.37kB gzip -- misleadingly named after seo.ts (a 39-line file) but Vite grouped a large vendor dependency (almost certainly 'motion'/Framer Motion, used across every page) into it, so every single route pays ~56kB gzip for a chunk whose name gives no clue what's actually in it -- worth renaming/splitting for maintainability. Per-route JS on top of that shared cost: homepage App.tsx = 53.81kB/11.95kB gzip (light). BY FAR the heaviest route: About.tsx = 416.52kB/156.92kB gzip -- more than double every other route combined, almost certainly the dotted-map Southeast Asia map component (CLAUDE.md's 2026-09-07 session note) plus its SVG/data payload. All other feature-detail pages are small (6-18kB gzip each). REAL NETWORK MEASUREMENT (localhost, via Performance/Resource Timing APIs after npm run build + vite preview): homepage first-paint/first-contentful-paint = ~3028ms in this sandboxed browser-automation environment -- flagged as a single data point from a non-representative environment (local dev machine, automation overhead, no CDN/compression tuning), not a substitute for a real Lighthouse/PageSpeed Insights run. /about total network transfer measured at ~309KB in a single navigation, including a 153.7KB video (public/assets/animated-edii.mp4) that loads unconditionally -- src/app/About.tsx's VideoMascot component sets autoPlay+loop+muted+playsInline with no preload/lazy control, so the browser fetches it immediately regardless of scroll position (MEDIUM finding: video is already well-optimized in absolute terms per the 2026-09-07 session, 4.6MB->153KB, but nothing defers it off the critical initial-load path). IMPORTANT LIMITATION, disclosed rather than worked around: true Core Web Vitals (LCP, CLS, TBT) could NOT be captured -- the browser-automation tool's tab reports document.visibilityState='hidden'/hasFocus=false even when fronted, and the browser spec correctly suppresses largest-contentful-paint and layout-shift PerformanceObserver entries for backgrounded tabs, so getEntriesByType returned empty for both across repeated attempts. This is a tooling limitation of the sandboxed preview, not a site issue -- recommend Kenneth or a future session run Chrome DevTools Lighthouse (or PageSpeed Insights once a public preview URL exists) directly for authoritative LCP/CLS/TBT scores; the bundle-size and network-transfer data above is real and reliable, the timing-based Web Vitals are not available from this environment. MAJOR BOTTLENECKS RECORDED (ranked by impact): 1) About.tsx's 157kB-gzip route chunk (map component) -- single biggest lever if About-page performance matters for Singapore users on slower connections. 2) The misleadingly-named seo-*.js shared chunk (56kB gzip on every page) -- a naming/chunking hygiene issue worth fixing when p1-t2's build tooling changes are implemented anyway. 3) fbevents.js (Meta Pixel, third-party, 106.4KB observed) loads on every page via GTM -- outside this repo's direct control per CLAUDE.md's existing GTM/Consent-Mode notes, but a real weight contributor. 4) About page's autoplay video is not deferred off the critical path. Also noted in passing (not SEO-scoped, flagging for awareness only): `npm install` reported 1 high-severity dependency vulnerability -- not investigated further here, out of scope for an SEO/GEO audit, `npm audit` would show details if Kenneth wants it looked at separately. `npm run build` itself is otherwise clean -- no chunk-size warnings, no typecheck errors, no dead-route surprises.

p2-t10.notes: Confirmed the underlying cause: vercel.json's blanket '/(.*) -> /index.html' rewrite meant literally every URL, including nonexistent ones, returned HTTP 200 -- a true soft-404 (NotFound.tsx does set noindex client-side, but only after JS runs, and the HTTP status itself was always 200 regardless). FIX IMPLEMENTED (does not require the p3-t1 prerender work first -- this is safe and effective standing alone): narrowed vercel.json's rewrites from one catch-all pattern to an explicit list matching only the 9 real route patterns in main.tsx (/, /features, /features-new, /features/:slug [covers all 7 feature-detail pages including the dynamic ai one], /pricing, /contact, /about, /privacy, /terms). Any path that doesn't match one of these now falls through to Vercel's normal static-file behavior instead of being force-rewritten to index.html. Added public/404.html (a small, dependency-free static page -- brand navy/blue, the real logo, 'Page not found', a Home link, noindex meta) so that fallthrough serves something presentable; Vite copies public/ verbatim so this becomes dist/404.html, which is Vercel's documented convention for a custom error page served with a genuine 404 status. WHY THIS DOESN'T BREAK ANYTHING: every real route (all 15 concrete paths + the 6 feature slugs) still explicitly matches a rewrite rule and continues to work exactly as before on direct load/refresh -- I checked this route-by-route against main.tsx's <Routes> before writing the rule list, specifically to avoid the much worse regression of breaking direct navigation to a real page. REMAINING GAP, disclosed rather than glossed over: a typo'd slug under /features/ (e.g. /features/typo) still matches the /features/:slug rewrite and gets a client-side NotFound at HTTP 200 -- a much smaller, already-noindexed edge case than before, not eliminated entirely; that full fix is still owned by p3-t1's prerendering work as p1-t2 already decided. VERIFICATION LIMITATION, disclosed: I could not test the actual HTTP-status behavior against real Vercel infrastructure -- vite preview doesn't emulate vercel.json's rewrites, and running `vercel dev` would require linking this unlinked project to a Vercel account/project, which I did not do without Kenneth's involvement (that's deploy-adjacent account action, not something to do unilaterally). What IS verified: vercel.json is valid JSON, `npm run build` produces dist/404.html correctly, and the rewrite-narrowing follows Vercel's standard, widely-documented rewrites + static-fallback + custom-404.html pattern. Recommend confirming the real HTTP status codes once this reaches an actual Vercel preview deployment.

p3-t1.notes: Implemented the Puppeteer approach decided in p1-t2. CORRECTION to that earlier decision: it recommended puppeteer-core + @sparticuz/chromium, based on guidance for Vercel *serverless functions* (which have a 250MB deploy-size limit); this prerender step runs as a *build* step (extends `npm run build`), which executes in Vercel's full build container, not a constrained function runtime -- so plain `puppeteer` (bundles its own compatible Chromium, simpler, standard for build-time prerendering) is actually the right choice here. Installed and test-launched real headless Chromium locally first to confirm feasibility before writing anything -- it worked immediately. BUILT: scripts/prerender.mjs, wired into package.json's build script (`vite build && node scripts/prerender.mjs`). It hand-rolls a minimal static file server (Node http, explicit 127.0.0.1 binding) rather than using vite's preview() JS API -- that API's default host binding produced ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED against Chrome's --host-resolver-rules override (an IPv4/IPv6 loopback mismatch: vite preview's 'localhost' bind and my 127.0.0.1 DNS override were technically both 'localhost' but different addresses, so nothing was listening where Chrome connected) -- switching to an explicit, unambiguous bind fixed it immediately. CRITICAL BUG CAUGHT DURING THIS TASK (would have deindexed the entire live site if shipped): the first working version of the script baked noindex,nofollow into every single route including the homepage. Root cause: src/app/seo.ts's isReviewHost() correctly checks window.location.hostname against PRODUCTION_HOSTS and forces noindex on anything else (existing, deliberate safety net against indexing a Vercel preview URL) -- but during local prerendering the hostname is necessarily 'localhost', which fails that check same as any other non-production host would. FIX: launch Puppeteer with --host-resolver-rules mapping edbuddies.ai (and www) to 127.0.0.1, and navigate via http://edbuddies.ai:<port>/... instead of localhost -- so window.location.hostname genuinely reads 'edbuddies.ai' during capture and the app's existing, unmodified hostname logic does the right thing. Did NOT touch seo.ts's hostname logic itself to work around this -- fixing it in the prerender script's navigation target instead preserves that logic exactly as designed. Verified this fix works: every real route's captured HTML now says index,follow; /features-new (deliberately included in the prerender list despite being noindex, since it's a real linked page that must keep working on direct load/refresh) still correctly says noindex,nofollow -- its own explicit setPageMeta({noindex:true}) call overrides regardless of host. IMPORTANT SAFETY NOTE for Phase 3/beyond: this build-time capture bakes 'production' assumptions into the static HTML on every build, including a future Vercel PREVIEW deployment build (which would run this same build script) -- so a preview URL's static files would ALSO say index,follow at parse time. This is safe ONLY because the inline hostname-check <script> in index.html is captured verbatim into every generated file (confirmed: present in both dist/index.html and dist/features/enrolment/index.html) and re-runs live in any real visitor's browser, correctly flipping to noindex for any non-production hostname regardless of what was baked in at build time -- full detail and the preview-deployment review itself is in p3-t3's notes, please read together with this entry. ALSO CHANGED: vercel.json's rewrites array (added in p2-t10) is now REMOVED entirely -- with real static files now existing for every route, Vercel's default static-file serving resolves them correctly with no rewrite needed, and removing the rewrites means genuinely unknown paths fall through to the real dist/404.html automatically, which is cleaner and more correct than maintaining an allowlist that could drift out of sync with main.tsx over time (exactly what p1-t2's original writeup predicted would happen once this task shipped). KNOWN, DELIBERATE TRADE-OFF not fixed here: src/main.tsx still uses createRoot (not hydrateRoot), so a real browser's React will replace the prerendered DOM with a fresh client-render on mount rather than truly hydrating it -- a brief flash of prerendered content, then a normal client render, not broken but not optimal. Switching to hydrateRoot was deliberately NOT attempted: it requires the server/prerendered markup to match React's first client render almost exactly or React logs mismatches and falls back anyway, and Framer Motion's animated initial states (opacity:0 etc. before animating in) make that a real, untested risk -- out of proportion to what this task needed (crawlable static HTML, which is fully achieved either way). Verified: full clean `npm run build` (typecheck + vite build + prerender) succeeds end to end, all 15 routes generate successfully, repeated 3 times across iterations while debugging with consistent results.
